name: Sine Wave
description: Fundamental oscillation pattern and superposition basis for all periodic phenomena. Any complex signal can be decomposed into sine wave components via Fourier analysis. Governed by tau (2pi), the natural period constant.

scope.definition: Fraction of periodic functions expressible as convergent Fourier series of sine and cosine components — measured by Dirichlet condition coverage across standard function classes.

evidence.source: Fourier (1822) 'Théorie Analytique de la Chaleur'; Dirichlet (1829) convergence conditions proof; modern treatment in Stein & Shakarchi (2003) 'Fourier Analysis', Princeton UP.
cross_domain_examples: Dirichlet theorem: any piecewise smooth periodic function has a convergent Fourier series — mathematically proven
heat equation: Fourier series solution to PDE is exact, not approximate — mathematical identity
quantum mechanics: energy eigenstates form complete orthonormal basis — generalizes Fourier decomposition
signal processing: DFT decomposes any finite digital sequence exactly into sinusoidal components

scope.falsifiability: If a piecewise continuous periodic function is found whose Fourier series diverges everywhere, Dirichlet's theorem has a counterexample — no such function has ever been found.
scope.measurement_limits: Fourier series converge to function values at continuity points; at discontinuities they converge to the midpoint (Gibbs phenomenon near jumps). For non-periodic functions, Fourier transforms rather than series are required.
